map.emptyInventory: No nodes in the inventory yet.

note.level: Connectivity graph — links discovered from CDP/LLDP adjacency, shared IP subnets and routing. Each subfolder is drawn as one box; select a box to go into it.

empty.level: Nothing on this level has a discovered link yet. Links come from CDP/LLDP adjacency and from nodes sharing an IP subnet, so the map fills in as those walks run.

map.folderTitle: {{name}} — {{count}} nodes, worst: {{state}}. Select to go in.
map.externalTitle: Links to {{name}}, outside this folder. Select to open the level where both ends are shown.
map.edgeTitle: {{count}} links ({{source}}). Select to list the ports.

overflow.title: Too many to draw on one level
overflow.body: This level has {{count}} linked nodes directly in it, and one level draws at most {{max}}. Its subfolders are still shown below; moving nodes into subfolders makes the level drawable.
overflow.openNodes: Open this folder in the node list

dependency.note: Manage the dependency graph: each node's upstream drives parent-down alert suppression and root-cause roll-up. The Network map visualizes the same edges.
dependency.emptyInventory: No nodes in the inventory yet.
dependency.emptyFiltered: No matching nodes — adjust the search or filter.

verdictHelp.agree: Both graphs give this node the same upstreams.
verdictHelp.only_manual: Set by hand but not discovered. Switching to the derived graph would drop this dependency, so this node's alert would stop rolling up.
verdictHelp.only_derived: Discovered but never set by hand. Switching to the derived graph would add this dependency — this is the direction that can suppress a real outage, so check it.
verdictHelp.unmodelled: Neither graph gives this node an upstream, so its alert always stands on its own.

mode.label: Suppression follows
mode.manualNote: Alert suppression follows each node's hand-authored upstream. Switch to Comparing to see what the discovered graph would do, without changing anything.
mode.shadowNote: Alerting is unchanged — this is a preview. The table below shows where the two graphs differ, and how many active alerts would change.
mode.derivedNote: Alert suppression follows the graph discovered from CDP/LLDP adjacency and shared subnets. Editing a node's upstream by hand no longer affects suppression.
mode.revert: Go back to the hand-authored graph
mode.blocked: Cannot use the derived graph yet: {{pools}} has nodes but no poller that could be placed in the graph. Set an anchor node for its poller under Settings ▸ Pollers first.
mode.wouldSuppress_one: {{count}} active alert would newly be suppressed.
mode.wouldSuppress_other: {{count}} active alerts would newly be suppressed.
mode.wouldUnsuppress_one: {{count}} active alert would stop being suppressed.
mode.wouldUnsuppress_other: {{count}} active alerts would stop being suppressed.
mode.reviewFirst: Review the alerts that would newly be suppressed before switching — each of those is an alert that would stop being raised.
mode.noChange: No active alert's suppression would change.
mode.coverage: {{covered}} of {{total}} nodes would get an upstream

dependency.optOutHelp: Excluded from derived suppression: this node's alert always stands on its own, whatever the discovered graph says. Only ever removes suppression, so it cannot hide an outage.
dependency.editHiddenInDerived: The upstream is discovered in this mode, so it is not edited here. Correct a wrong link on the Network map instead.

geo.title: Geo map
geo.subtitle: Sites placed by their group coordinates, coloured by worst member state.
geo.empty: No group has coordinates yet. Set latitude and longitude on a group under Nodes ▸ its Edit dialog, and it appears here.
geo.resize: Drag to resize the map (double-click to reset)
